answer: Latency histogram fingerprinting: each agent identity must maintain a rolling arrival-time distribution across its request stream, and the system flags identities whose inter-arrival variance falls below organic baseline—a reef of synchronized bursts stands out. Traffic shape is checked against a copper reference curve of genuine human-paced sessions, so cloned identities produce a telltale signal of too-regular spacing. An attacker must inject randomized delays and jitter per identity, multiplying coordination cost by the number of sybils and slowing each one below useful throughput.
